scope: Shared 10-case comparison. This is a static retrieval snapshot of the initial good..bad interval, not a runner-step table. T1/T2/T3 never shrink the live bisect window.
t3_definition: T3 = T2 ∩ commits that touch the top-20% usage files of one grep anchor. T2 = T1 ∩ (stack symbols ∪ pass names ∪ crash file). T1 = keywords ∪ relevant_paths ∪ high_risk_paths.
honest_anchor_policy: Most-specific real grep term: fewest files in llvm/lib + llvm/include. No first-bad SHA, no gtIncluded peek. This is the policy a runtime filter would actually run.
study_anchor_policy: dep-analysis.js line 269: first top20 variant with gtIncluded, else anchors[0]. That pick is GT-conditioned and is not a runtime method.
invalid_reason: Offline GT-checked leftover sizes, not runner steps. Honest T3 is a hard-cut experiment on the initial interval. It is not a BCR/git-bisect lane.

aggregate.note: The published 14-commit leftovers are study T3, not honest T3. Honest T3 already drops GT on the two MemorySSA checker cases.

code_analysis.first_bad_subject: [SimpleLoopUnswitch] Generalize the notion of trivial unswitching (#193989)
code_analysis.patch_contact: The first-bad only edits SimpleLoopUnswitch.cpp. The new latch-unswitch path rewrites CFG (delete branch-to-latch, insert branch-to-unique-latch-exit) and then calls MSSAU->applyUpdates(Updates, DT). It never names verifyOptResult or ClobberWalker.
code_analysis.why_gt_out: Honest T3 greps the most-specific crash term verifyOptResult. That string lives only in MemorySSA.cpp (the detector). SimpleLoopUnswitch.cpp has zero mentions, so gtRank is empty and T3 collapses to the 6 interval commits that touch MemorySSA.cpp. The producer is one layer up: unswitch dirties MemorySSA through the updater API; LICM later walks clobbers and the checker fires.
code_analysis.mechanism: checker-vs-producer. Crash file is the detector, not the first-bad.

code_analysis.first_bad_subject: [SimpleLoopUnswitch] Generalize the notion of trivial unswitching (#193989)
code_analysis.patch_contact: Identical first-bad SHA and compact diff as pr204559. The new code calls MSSAU->applyUpdates. Unswitch later also goes through MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks, which then calls removeFromLookups. SimpleLoopUnswitch.cpp never contains the string removeFromLookups.
code_analysis.why_gt_out: Honest T3 greps removeFromLookups. Heavy use is one file, MemorySSAUpdater.cpp; top20 therefore has 1 interval commit and no SimpleLoopUnswitch.cpp. The first-bad is still the unswitch CFG/latch rewrite. removeFromLookups is an internal MemorySSA helper that fires when a later block-removal sees a MemoryAccess that still has uses — a stale graph left by applyUpdates, not a change inside MemorySSAUpdater.cpp.
code_analysis.mechanism: checker-vs-producer. Same enabling commit as pr204559; a different MemorySSA invariant is the detector because the reproducer runs at -O3 with nontrivial unswitch.
